newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada '96 manufacturing outlook negative - StatsCan.
newsitem.headline: Canada '96 manufacturing outlook negative - StatsCan.

text.p: Labor disputes in the automotive industry caused Canada's manufacturing production outlook to turn negative for the rest of 1996, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
In its quarterly survey of business conditions, completed in October, the agency said manufacturers' balance of opinion for production prospects fell 19 points to -12.
The number was calculated by subtracting the 34 percent who stated that production prospects for the coming three months were lower from the 22 percent who said they expected higher production.
Statistics Canada said the downturn in expectations was partly offset by fairly positive results in the electrical and electronics products and the machinery industries.
"If the decline in transportation equipment were excluded, production prospects would have been positive for the rest of manufacturing," the agency said.

It said manufacturers were less concerned about finished-product inventories and were still positive about new orders. In addition, more manufacturers were expected to increase their workforce in the coming three months.

A record 77 percent of manufacturers said they expected little change in their workforce. The number who said they would cut employment fell to 10 percent in October from 13 percent in the July survey.
Because of a 20-day strike at General Motors Corp's Canadian unit, only 78 percent of manufacturers said they had no production problems at this time.
